items.title: Canadian Dollar futures rebound as U.S. hiring cools.
items.excerpt: Canadian Dollar futures rotated higher after three consecutive sessions of losses, buoyed by a widening Canadian trade surplus and weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data. Statistics Canada reported the June merchandise trade surplus expanded to 3.86 billion Canadian dollars, driven by a 16.5% surge in metals and mineral exports led by gold. In the U.S., ADP private payrolls grew by just 44,000, while ISM Services employment slipped into contraction territory. The combination of soft U.S. labor data and persistent inflation pressure weighed on the greenback, providing support for the loonie.

items.title: Australian Dollar futures rebound toward multi-month highs.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming discusses the recent price action in Australian Dollar futures, highlighting a swift recovery from recent selling pressure. The currency is demonstrating relative strength compared to other major FX markets, largely driven by stronger-than-expected Australian household data and persistent weakness in the U.S. dollar. Deming notes that the Australian dollar is pushing toward one-and-a-half-month highs, with 0.706 acting as the next critical upside target. A successful breakout above this level could drive prices to their highest point since early June. The broader currency complex remains somewhat mixed, though most majors are leaning higher against the softer greenback.

Geopolitical complexities further complicate the supply picture, particularly following the breakdown of the preliminary U.S.-Iran agreement and potential disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Traders will evaluate how these supply-side factors, combined with a heavy week of earnings and critical U.S. labor data, drive market action next week.

items.title: Canadian Dollar futures recovered losses on strong GDP.
items.excerpt: September Canadian Dollar futures recovered midday losses to trade down slightly by 0.22%, staying on track for a weekly gain of roughly 0.5%. The currency found support following stronger-than-expected economic data, as Canada's May GDP grew 0.3%—beating the 0.1% forecast—driven by 1% growth in mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction. Second-quarter GDP growth is currently estimated at an annualized pace of 3.4%, well above the Bank of Canada's 2.5% projection. While robust economic performance reduces the likelihood of near-term rate cuts by the Bank of Canada, a 125 to 150 basis point yield advantage in U.S. interest rates continues to keep pressure on the currency.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures surged on suspected intervention.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures posted their largest single-day gain in 4 years, rallying 2.75% to reach a 2-month high. The sharp move higher broke a persistent 3-month downtrend that had weighed on the currency since mid-May, pushing prices to their highest levels since June 1. Market participants attributed the surge primarily to potential intervention by the Japanese Ministry of Finance. Broader currency market dynamics also provided support, as the U.S. Dollar weakened across the board in the wake of the Federal Reserve's latest policy messaging. The rally extended across major G10 currencies, with the British pound, euro, and Australian dollar also booking solid gains.
